concepts.title: Composition of the Atmosphere: Gases, Vapour and Particulates
concepts.definition: The atmosphere is a mixture of nitrogen about 78 per cent, oxygen about 21 per cent, argon, carbon dioxide and traces of other gases, along with water vapour and dust particulates, which together absorb heat, sustain life and shape weather.
concepts.key_idea: Carbon dioxide and water vapour are the heat absorbing gases of the atmosphere, and particulates act as condensation nuclei for clouds.

concepts.title: Structure of the Atmosphere: Troposphere to Exosphere
concepts.definition: The atmosphere is layered into the troposphere where weather occurs and temperature falls with height, the stratosphere holding the ozone layer, the mesosphere, the thermosphere or ionosphere reflecting radio waves, and the exosphere merging into space, separated by pauses of equal temperature.
concepts.key_idea: The tropopause, stratopause and mesopause mark the boundaries, and the ozone layer in the stratosphere shields life from ultraviolet radiation.

concepts.title: Weather, Climate and the Role of the Atmosphere for Life
concepts.definition: The atmosphere shields the earth from harmful ultraviolet rays, holds oxygen for breathing and carbon dioxide for plants, and through its water vapour and heat absorbing gases keeps the planet warm enough for life, while its motions produce weather and climate.
concepts.key_idea: Human activities that alter atmospheric composition, as in ozone depletion and greenhouse gas build up, directly threaten this life support system.
